final_answer:
Differential expression between ALS and control cervical spinal cord identified 180 genes at FDR < 0.05 and |log2FC| >= 1: 114 up-regulated in ALS and 66 down-regulated in ALS.

The strongest ALS-upregulated genes were dominated by microglial/macrophage, lysosomal, and lipid/inflammatory markers, including GPNMB (log2FC 2.81, FDR 6.65e-22), ASAH1 (1.05, FDR 2.26e-19), IQGAP2 (1.71, FDR 1.22e-18), ACP5 (1.48, FDR 2.45e-18), CTSS (1.60, FDR 3.15e-18), APOC1 (2.05, FDR 5.29e-18), LYZ (2.33, FDR 5.29e-18), PLA2G7 (1.93, FDR 4.19e-17), APOE (1.17, FDR 9.69e-17), CD48 (1.64, FDR 2.00e-16), MS4A7 (1.48, FDR 7.52e-16), LGALS3 (1.37, FDR 7.95e-16), MSR1 (1.63, FDR 1.78e-15), and CHIT1 (3.33, FDR 7.55e-15).

The down-regulated genes included neuronal/synaptic and ion-channel/neurofilament genes such as SHANK3 (log2FC -1.03, FDR 5.36e-10), CACNA1B (-1.13, FDR 7.54e-9), GRIN1 (-1.51, FDR 1.56e-3), SHANK1 (-1.34, FDR 1.78e-5), KCNT1 (-1.29, FDR 1.06e-5), NEFH (-1.27, FDR 1.69e-3), NEFL (-1.27, FDR 1.13e-2), CPLX1 (-1.24, FDR 2.85e-4), and CPLX2 (-1.24, FDR 3.03e-3).

Overall, the cervical spinal cord ALS transcriptome shows strong glial/innate-immune and phagolysosomal activation with concurrent loss of neuronal and synaptic expression programs. Full results are in outputs/ALS_vs_Control_cervical_logCPM_covariate_lm.csv.
